stops.note: named a member of the priestly class
stops.meaning: a Hindu priest of the highest caste

stops.note: Greek writers described the Indian priest-philosophers they encountered
Roman and medieval Latin writers preserved the Greek term
Portuguese traders in India carried the word to Europe
borrowed into French before reaching English
settled as the English term for the priestly caste, later extended to any elite class
stops.meaning: a member of the priestly Hindu caste; loosely, a person of high standing

current_meaning: A member of the highest Hindu priestly caste; loosely, a person of refined, elite social standing.
